name: Baked Cheddar Chicken Thighs with Mushrooms, Bell Peppers & Broccoli

instructions.primary_message: Place spices in a large bowl and stir to combine.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ tsp onion powder
1 ½ tsp garlic powder
1 ½ tsp rosemary, dried
1 ½ tsp thyme, dried
1 ½ tsp salt
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Preheat a large pot over medium heat.
While the pot heats up, pat chicken dry with paper towels and place on a plate. Sprinkle half of the spices over both sides to coat. (Reserve remaining spice mix for the veggies.)

Once the pot is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Working in batches if necessary, add the chicken and cook until golden brown and almost cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Remove to a clean plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil. (Reserve pot with cooking juices for later use.)
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 caps portobello mushrooms
3 red bell peppers
3 crowns broccoli

instructions.primary_message: Remove mushroom stems and carefully scrape out the gills. Medium dice and add to the bowl with the remaining spice mix.
Trim, seed, and medium dice bell peppers; add to the bowl.
Separate broccoli into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces. Add to the bowl.
Return pot to medium heat. Add more butter and swirl to coat the bottom; add veggies and remaining spice mix. Cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies soften, 7-8 minutes.
Meanwhile, cut cream cheese into small pieces. Coarsely grate cheddar.
instructions.secondary_message:
¾ (227 g) block cream cheese
¾ (227 g) block cheddar cheese

instructions.primary_message: When the veggies are soft, add cream cheese to the pot; cook, stirring frequently, until melted and combined.
Transfer veggie mixture to a large baking dish; nestle chicken into the veggies and top with cheddar. Place in the oven and bake until cheese is melted and chicken is cooked through, 8-10 minutes.
To serve, divide cheesy chicken and veggies between plates or bowls. Enjoy!
